summary: FieldShift is a climate-aware crop-planning decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Users outline a field on a map; the app combines NASA POWER daily climate data and long-term climatology with modelled ISRIC SoilGrids properties and other available forecast and market sources. It compares 27 crop profiles, presenting transparent rule-based scores, confidence in data completeness, and visible risks such as heat, rainfall, water demand, pests, soil limits, and price uncertainty. Users can also explore climate conditions, irrigation, crop rotations, soil health, and illustrative gross-value scenarios. FieldShift turns public Earth-observation and agricultural data into an understandable starting point for local planning, helping users ask better questions about changing conditions. It is decision support, not an agronomic guarantee, yield forecast, or financial advice.
details:
FieldShift is a browser-based decision-support tool for climate-aware crop planning. Users draw a field boundary on a map, then review available climate, soil, forecast, and market context. The app compares 27 crop profiles using transparent, rule-based scores and shows risks and data-confidence labels. Confidence describes how complete the available inputs are; it is not the probability of a successful harvest. Other tools help users explore climate trends, irrigation, soil health, pests, crop rotations, and illustrative gross-value scenarios.

NASA POWER daily climate data and long-term climatology provide the core NASA data. FieldShift also uses modelled ISRIC SoilGrids data and other available forecast and market sources. The interface brings these different inputs together so users can see the reasoning, sources, dates, assumptions, and limitations behind the guidance.

We built FieldShift with Python and FastAPI for the backend, JavaScript for the browser interface, SQLite for data storage, and Docker for deployment. The team considered data availability and age, the different spatial scales of the datasets, local water and soil conditions, crop risks, and market uncertainty. Its creative approach is to turn public Earth and agricultural data into an explainable field-planning workflow. The intended impact is to help farmers and planners explore options and ask better local questions as climate conditions change. FieldShift is a planning aid, not an agronomic guarantee, yield forecast, or financial advice.
